descriptionChirho: Temporal perpetuity directed toward the future, meaning 'forever, evermore,' often in the idiom לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד 'forever and ever' or standing alone as לָעַד 'for ever.'
Prepositional use indicating a spatial or temporal endpoint or limit, meaning 'to, unto, until, as far as, up to.'
Past-directed temporal reference meaning 'of old, from antiquity,' denoting a time in the remote past.
The abstract noun sense of boundless or unending time, 'eternity,' without specific past or future orientation.
Used as the nomen rectum in the messianic title אֲבִי־עַד 'Father of Eternity' (Isa 9:5), designating everlasting dominion.
